item.text: I found a better seam for the cleanup: the async handlers are still peeling `telemetryContext.attributes()` off just to hand it straight to `SearchResponseMetrics`. I’m checking the metrics API now so I can add overloads that take the context directly and remove that repetition from the handlers.

I’m collapsing the last repeated accessor pattern into `SearchResponseMetrics` itself. That lets the async handlers pass the telemetry bundle as a whole instead of peeling out the attribute map for each metric call.

The core handlers now hand the bundle directly to the metrics layer. I’m checking for any leftover `.attributes()` calls in the async path so I can remove the remaining boilerplate or confirm it’s only needed where the raw map is actually mutated.
The last pass is just to make sure the overloads didn’t introduce any signature drift or formatting issues. After that I’ll summarize exactly what got simplified in the async handlers.
I’m cleaning up the new public overloads now. They need short Javadocs, and I’m also trimming a couple of repeated `attributes()` reads inside the metrics helpers while I’m there.

Streamlined the async telemetry path so the handlers pass `SearchTelemetryContext` directly into the metrics layer instead of unpacking attributes at each call site.
